propositions: Prompt cache breakpoint is positioned after pass-specific stance suffixes rather than at the shared plan-prefix boundary, causing different cache keys across passes within a single run despite byte-identical leading content.

Cache write operations occur on every plan-review call but reads never occur within single-turn pass executions, resulting in premium-rate write billing (~9-11k tokens per review) with zero discount-rate reads.
The diagnostic warn_if_cache_ineffective detects only write==0 AND read==0 patterns and misses the write-every-call-never-read shape that occurs in plan-review passes.
Moving the cache breakpoint to the end of shared_plan_prefix enables the Pass-1 finder write to be read by Pass-2 verifier within the same run, and same-ticket re-reviews within TTL to hit the cache.

The marked prefix necessarily embeds the full plan text by design (for within-run container/chunk reuse), so cross-ticket cache identity is structurally impossible without destroying warm-then-fan-out reuse patterns.
